stem.en: A toy car of mass 250 g starts from rest on a track with no friction. It reaches 5 m/s in 2 s. What is the net force on it, in newtons?

correctFeedback.en: Correct — 250 g converts to 0.25 kg first, then F = ma = 0.25 × 2.5 = 0.625 N.

incorrectFeedback.en: Check your units before multiplying. F = ma needs mass in KILOGRAMS, not grams — using 250 directly (instead of converting to 0.25 kg) gives an answer exactly 1000× too large. If you got 625 N, that's the tell-tale sign of a forgotten gram-to-kilogram conversion. If you got a value around 1.25, double check a = (v − u) ÷ t first — a = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 m/s², not 5.

hints.en: Change 250 g into kg. Find a = (v - u) / t, then use F = ma.

explanation.en: First the acceleration: a = (5 m/s - 0) / 2 s = 2.5 m/s². The mass is 250 g = 0.25 kg. So F = ma = 0.25 kg x 2.5 m/s² = 0.625 N.
